BiblicalUsage: maqtsôwaʻ is a corner or angle, the join where walls meet. In Exodus 26:24 the boards of the tabernacle are coupled together for the two corners, and in Nehemiah 3:19 Ezer repairs another piece over against the going up to the armoury at the turning of the wall. The word is the corner that holds the building together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe maqtsôwaʻ shows me that even the corners of God's house are joined with care, and that no part of His work is careless.
